...HIGH RISK FOR EXTREME FIRE BEHAVIOR WITH ANY NEW FIRE STARTS
THURSDAY THROUGH SATURDAY DUE TO MODERATE TO LOCALLY STRONG SANTA
ANA WINDS AND LOW RELATIVE HUMIDITY...

.Moderate to locally strong Santa Ana winds will quickly develop
on Thursday, peak Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon,
then slowly weaken through the weekend. Meanwhile, dry air will
settle over the region and dry out any effects of the recent
rains. Red Flag Warnings are in effect for most of Los Angeles
and Ventura Counties Thursday through Saturday, and for interior
Santa Barbara and San Luis Obispo Counties for Friday.

Red Flag Warning for wind and low relative humidity, which is in
effect from 6 AM Thursday to 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* AFFECTED AREA...Antelope Valley Foothills.

* TIMING...From 6 AM Thursday to 8 PM PDT Saturday.

* WINDS...Northeast to east 20 to 30 mph with gusts of 40 to 50
mph, strongest Thursday afternoon through Friday afternoon.

* RELATIVE HUMIDITY...Minimums of 10 to 20 percent common.

* IMPACTS...If fire ignition occurs, conditions are favorable
for extreme fire behavior which would threaten life and
property.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions
are either occurring now, or will shortly. Use extreme caution
with anything that can spark a wildfire. Residents near wildland
interfaces should be prepared to evacuate if a wildfire breaks
out. See readyforwildfire.org and wildfirerisk.org for
information.

.With the ongoing drought conditions, we have KBDI values well into
the 700s, with 10-hour and 100-hour fuel moisture values hovering
around 25%. Subsidence behind the front will further dry out the
already dry continental air mass, leading to a significant drop in
dew points following the front. The forecast drops RH values below
30% across central Louisiana and the interior portions of
southeast Texas. Friday through Sunday look to be concerning for
fire weather. However, Saturday appears to be the most critical

highly dried out fuels. This setup is similar to the weather
conditions that sparked the Tiger Island fire in 2023, and fires
that do spark could quickly spread out of control..

properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 15 at 3:09AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W has been upgraded to Tropical Depression 29W, and is
currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 9.6N 161.2E. 29W will
continue to develop and strengthen just north of the region, and will
generally head towards the Marianas. Convergent fresh to strong
westerlies south of 29W's center are producing bands of scattered to
numerous showers capable of strong gusts and locally heavy rainfall,
across Pohnpei and their coastal waters, and Gusty winds across
Kosrae and their costal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests
rainfall amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei
through late Friday night as 29W strengthens and passes north of the
island. Gusts to 30 knots will be possible near heavier showers.
Moderate to strong winds with gusts to near-gale for Kosrae through
this afternoon as conditions start to ease there.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged.
For more information on TD 29W, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN32 PGTW and by the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ32 PGUM.

properties.areaDesc: Pohnpei Coastal Waters; Kosrae Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 14 at 4:17PM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
Invest 96W is currently rated as "High" for development by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center, and is the subject of a Tropical Cyclone
Formation Alert, meaning development into a significant tropical
cyclone (a tropical depression) is expected within 24 hours. 96W is
currently located northeast of Pohnpei near 8.7N 160.7E, and
continues to develop and strengthen just north of the region.
Convergent fresh to strong westerlies south of 96W's center are
producing bands of scattered to numerous showers capable of strong
gusts and locally heavy rainfall, across Kosrae, Pohnpei, and their
adjacent coastal waters. Ensemble model guidance suggests rainfall
amounts of 2 to 4 inches will be possible for Pohnpei through late
Friday night as 96W strengthens and passes north of the island, with
an additional 1 to 2 inches possible for Kosrae through early
Thursday morning as conditions start to ease there. Gusts to 30 knots
will be possible near heavier showers.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
hazardous to small craft, and inter-island travel is discouraged.
Keep up to date with the latest information from the National Weather
Service in Tiyan, Guam, and your local emergency management.
